title: Which Pharma Stock Looks More Attractive: Sanofi or AbbVie?
author: Na
description: Sanofi and AbbVie are compared as major pharmaceutical companies with different growth drivers. Sanofi, powered by Dupixent's strong performance and newer medicines, trades at a lower valuation (7.82x forward earnings) with a 4.5% dividend yield, while AbbVie relies on Skyrizi and Rinvoq to offset Humira's decline but trades at 19.62x forward earnings with a 2.5% yield. Analysts favor Sanofi (Zacks Rank #3 Hold) over AbbVie (Rank #4 Sell) due to its attractive valuation and upgraded growth outlook.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Sanofi receives a favorable recommendation due to attractive valuation (7.82x forward P/E vs. industry 21.77x), upgraded 2026 sales growth guidance to ~10%, strong Dupixent performance (€9.3B H1 sales, +28.6% YoY), expanding portfolio of newer medicines, and higher dividend yield (4.5%). Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates relative strength.

AbbVie receives a less favorable rating despite strong Skyrizi and Rinvoq performance due to higher valuation (19.62x forward P/E, above 5-year mean of 14.54), recent earnings estimate declines, competitive pressures from J&J's Icotyde, Humira biosimilar erosion, oncology slowdown, and lower dividend yield (2.5%). Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) reflects negative outlook.

Regeneron is mentioned as Sanofi's partner in Dupixent development but is not independently analyzed. The partnership's success is attributed to Sanofi's execution and market dynamics rather than Regeneron-specific factors.
J&J is mentioned as a competitive threat with its new psoriasis drug Icotyde, which increases pressure on AbbVie's Skyrizi. However, J&J is not independently evaluated in the analysis.

title: Why Did J&J Stock Fall After Q3 Earnings Despite Raised Guidance?
author: Na
description: Johnson & Johnson's shares fell 5.8% after Q3 2026 results showed earnings beat but sales missed expectations. MedTech segment underperformed with only 2.5% growth due to Abiomed declines and international market challenges, while Innovative Medicine remained strong. Despite headwinds, J&J raised full-year guidance and targets over $100 billion in 2026 revenue with accelerated growth expected in 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 5.8% despite earnings beat due to MedTech segment underperformance (2.5% growth vs. 7.7% for Innovative Medicine), Abiomed sales decline of 2.3%, international market disruptions, and adjusted EPS declining 7.5%. However, raised full-year guidance and confidence in 2026-2027 growth provide some offset.

title: JNJ Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Growth Outlook and MedTech Challenges
author: Na
description: Johnson & Johnson raised its 2026 sales guidance to $101-$101.4 billion and adjusted EPS to $11.05-$11.15, driven by strong Innovative Medicine growth of 7.9%, particularly from TREMFYA (up 68.3%) and DARZALEX (up 15.4%). However, MedTech underperformed with only 2.5% growth due to competitive pressures and international headwinds. The company expects $1.36 per share in acquisition-related earnings in 2027 and targets double-digit growth by decade-end.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with positive pharmaceutical segment growth and raised guidance offset by MedTech underperformance and weak price momentum. Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with unfavorable momentum score indicates near-term headwinds despite operational improvements.

title: UnitedHealth vs. Johnson & Johnson: Which Stock Is the Better Buy After Q3 Earnings?
author: Zacks.Com
description: UnitedHealth and Johnson & Johnson both raised full-year guidance after Q3 earnings, but with contrasting performance. UnitedHealth beat expectations with 60% YoY EPS growth driven by improved medical cost management, while J&J saw earnings decline 7.5% YoY despite pharmaceutical growth offsetting weak MedTech performance. UnitedHealth is recommended as the better buy due to stronger earnings momentum, lower valuation (19X vs 23X forward earnings), and higher dividend yield (2.45% vs 2%).

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q3 earnings beat (14% above consensus), 60% YoY EPS growth, improved medical cost ratio, raised full-year guidance above Wall Street expectations, lower valuation multiple, higher dividend yield, and Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with positive earnings estimate revisions support a positive outlook.

Mixed results with modest earnings beat (2% above consensus) but 7.5% YoY earnings decline, strong pharmaceutical division offset by weak MedTech performance, raised guidance but slightly below Street expectations, premium valuation, and Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) due to declining earnings estimates despite solid long-term fundamentals.

title: Stock Market Midday, Oct. 13: Bank Earnings and Chip Pressure Drive Mixed Trading
author: Emma Newbery
description: Major stock indexes traded mixed on October 13, 2026, as bank earnings kicked off the season with varied results and semiconductor stocks faced significant selling pressure. The S&P 500 fell 0.25%, the Nasdaq dropped 0.37%, and the Dow declined 0.18%. Goldman Sachs gained on strong earnings, while Wells Fargo and Johnson & Johnson declined on disappointing results. Semiconductor stocks, particularly Micron Technology, slid over 5% amid intensifying global competition and Chinese chip innovations.
